elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Article III is retained in full ("Licensor owns all right, title, and interest in and to the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein") and "DERIVATIVE WORK" sweeps in "any additions, modifications, improvements or enhancements"; the inserted clause grants only a licence ("Licensor grants Licensee a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license"), not ownership of the Article VII(b) customization work.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment language appears anywhere in the rendered text; the only operative grant is a licence in the new CUSTOMIZATION DELIVERABLES paragraph.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Article III is left untouched: "Licensee acknowledges that Licensor owns all right, title, and interest in and to the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein," and Licensed Technology comprises the Licensed Know-How and Licensed Software.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: "Notwithstanding Article III ... and Article XXI(a) and (b), Licensor grants Licensee a perpetual ... license to use, modify and sublicense ... all development and customization work performed for Licensee under Article VII(b)" — the customization work incorporates Licensed Technology, and the Article XXI(a) auto-termination is expressly overridden so the perpetual term is effective.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license", with the Article XXI(a) automatic licence termination and XXI(b) ship-back/certification expressly disapplied for this grant.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Grant is expressly "royalty-free"; the Article VII(b) pricing mechanic for commissioning the work is preserved and does not condition the licence on further royalties.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The insertion only limits any Licensor licence in Licensee data ("Any license granted to Licensor in data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Licensee is limited to processing that data solely to provide the services"); there is no affirmative sentence vesting or retaining right, title and interest in that data in Licensee.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: "Any license granted to Licensor in data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Licensee is limited to processing that data solely to provide the services under this Agreement" — the trigger covers every category of Licensee data and confines use to service delivery; no broader exploitation right is retained elsewhere.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Condition does not arise: no joint-ownership language exists in Article III, the Derivative Work definition, or the new clause; ownership sits solely with Licensor and Licensee's rights are purely licence-based.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Article III (retained unamended) confirms Licensor's ownership of the Licensed Technology, which by definition includes Licensed Know-How and the Platform Software; the new grant is expressly "Notwithstanding Article III" only as to the Article VII(b) customization work.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: "Licensor grants Licensee a perpetual ... license ... all development and customization work performed for Licensee under Article VII(b)", with Article XXI(a)'s automatic licence termination overridden by name so the perpetual term survives termination.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Grant is expressly "irrevocable"; the Article XXI(b) five-day ship-back and officer certification are disapplied for the Customization Deliverables, so nothing retained cancels or requires surrender of the licence.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "license to use, modify and sublicense, for Licensee's business", granted notwithstanding the Article II/VI use and no-modification restrictions and the Article III no-copy restriction, so no retained sentence contradicts it.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "use, modify and sublicense, for Licensee's business" — the sublicense right is express and the countervailing restrictions in Articles II, III and VI are named and overridden as to the Customization Deliverables.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Second sentence of the insertion confines any Licensor licence in "data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Licensee" to "processing that data solely to provide the services under this Agreement"; no distribution, resale or independent-exploitation right is retained.

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback level: all eight fallback elements are met by the inserted CUSTOMIZATION DELIVERABLES paragraph, which is scoped to the Article VII(b) work — the only deliverable/work product created for Licensee under this Agreement.

Preferred level fails on two operative gaps the drafter would have to repair if escalating: (i) no sentence vesting or assigning ownership of the Article VII(b) customization work (and the Derivative Works it constitutes) in Licensee, and (ii) no affirmative sentence retaining Licensee's right, title and interest in data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Licensee — the data sentence only caps Licensor's licence and ownership cannot be inferred from it.

Minimality holds: nothing is deleted, Article III's Licensor-favourable retained ownership, its infringement-enforcement rights, the Article VII(b) pricing mechanic and the balance of Article XXI survive. The notwithstanding override is not a blanket 'anything to the contrary' clause — it names Articles II, III, VI and XXI(a)/(b) only, and each is genuinely necessary (Articles II/III/VI to unlock use, modification, copying and sublicensing; XXI(a)/(b) to prevent automatic licence termination and ship-back from defeating the perpetual/irrevocable elements). No survival tail, expense allocation, procedure or extra damages category is added.
Minor drafting note, not a minimality failure: the defined term "Customization Deliverables" is created but never used again; it could be dropped without loss.

Intent is preserved: no dangling cross-reference or undefined trigger is introduced (Article VII(b) remains the commissioning mechanic, and the licence simply attaches to work actually performed under it), and the named overrides prevent the retained Article XXI sentences from contradicting the new grant.

Finding classification of 'deviation' is correct — the pre-redline clause failed the fallback outright (no perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free use/modify/sublicense licence to what Licensee pays for, and the licence terminated automatically under Article XXI(a)).
